correctness.rationale: Over characteristic two, substitution proves the quartic equation. The quadratic map is finite because it pulls back O(1) to ample O(2), and birational via the Cremona inverse on XYZ nonzero. Explicit integral-module identities give the reduced conductor off the triple point; the three smooth transverse branches give its conductor at the triple point. The unique pole of v²+v=1/w has order one and different exponent two. Exact differential minors give length-two schemes at three points. The triangle/concurrent-line counts and absolute-trace criterion prove the formulas for all q=2^m. Independent finite-field enumeration for q=2,4,8,16 corroborates the formula but does not replace the argument.

value.rationale: For a classical natural projection of the Veronese surface, the result identifies a sharp characteristic-two transition from six tame pinch points to three length-two wild degeneracies and gives a complete Artin–Schreier description of the nonnormal double lines. The exact missing-image formula and absolute-trace criterion for every binary extension resolve a practical ambiguity between points on a rational surface and points represented by its quadratic normalization parametrization. The conductor and ramification data are geometric, rather than a routine small-field enumeration.
